questions.question: Which scientist first coined the term, Ecosystem/Ecological System?

• **Educated **at **Highgate School**, **University College London**, and **Trinity College, Cambridge**, **Tansley taught **at these universities and at **Oxford**, where he **served as Sherardian Professor of Botany **until **his retirement in 1937**.
 
• He was **born on 15 August 1871 in London**, **United Kingdom**, and died on **25 November 1955 **in **Grantchester, United Kingdom**

questions.question: In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Project Tiger** was launched by the Government of India on **1st April 1973**.
 
• The aim of this initiative was to ensure a viable population of Bengal tigers in their natural habitats and to protect them from extinction.
 
• This project is administered by the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).
 
• Initially, nine tiger reserves were covered under this project, which has now expanded to cover more than 50 tiger reserves across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**

 
 
• The NTCA was constituted under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2006, for strengthening tiger conservation.
 
• It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
 
• The NTCA is responsible for the implementation of Project Tiger to ensure the protection of tigers.
 
• It regularly assesses tiger populations, habitat status, and the success of conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**
 
 
• This Act was enacted by the Indian Parliament to ensure the protection of wild animals, birds, and plants.
 
• It aims to safeguard the country's ecological and environmental security.
 
• The Act provides for the creation of protected areas such as national parks and wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• It also lays down the legal framework for the protection and management of wildlife habitats.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Bengal Tigers**
 
 
• Bengal tigers (Panthera tigris tigris) are native to the Indian subcontinent and are classified as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
 
• Efforts to conserve Bengal tigers include anti-poaching measures, habitat restoration, and community involvement.
 
• India is home to more than 70% of the world's wild tiger population.
 
• Effective conservation strategies have led to an increase in the tiger population in recent years.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a greenhouse gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitric oxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nitric oxide (NO)** is not considered a greenhouse gas because it does not have a significant impact on the Earth's temperature or climate.
 
• Greenhouse gases are those that can absorb and emit infrared radiation, leading to the greenhouse effect. Nitric oxide does not significantly contribute to this process.
 
• Common greenhouse gases include **carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O)**, all of which have a much higher potential to trap heat in the atmosphere.
 
• Nitric oxide is primarily known for its role in the formation of smog and its impact on the respiratory system, rather than its role as a greenhouse gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Greenhouse Gases:**

 
 
• Greenhouse gases are those gases in the Earth's atmosphere that trap heat. They allow sunlight to enter the atmosphere freely, but when the Earth's surface emits the energy back as infrared radiation (heat), greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit this radiation, warming the planet.
 
• The primary greenhouse gases in Earth's atmosphere are water vapor (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and ozone (O3).
 
• Human activities, such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, and industrial processes, have significantly increased the concentrations of these greenhouse gases, leading to global warming and climate change.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO2):**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is a colorless, odorless gas that is essential for plant life through the process of photosynthesis.
 
• It is produced by the combustion of fossil fuels, deforestation, and various industrial processes.
 
• CO2 is the most significant long-lived greenhouse gas in Earth's atmosphere, contributing to global warming and climate change.
 
 
 
• **Methane (CH4):**
 
 
• Methane is a potent greenhouse gas with a global warming potential many times greater than that of CO2 over a 20-year period.
 
• It is produced naturally through the decomposition of organic matter and human activities such as livestock farming, rice cultivation, and landfills.
 
• Despite its shorter atmospheric lifetime compared to CO2, methane's impact on global warming is substantial.
 
 
 
• **Nitrous Oxide (N2O):**
 
 
• Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas that is more effective than CO2 at trapping heat in the atmosphere over a 100-year period.
 
• It is emitted from agricultural and industrial activities, as well as during the combustion of fossil fuels and solid waste.
 
• N2O also plays a role in the depletion of the ozone layer in the stratosphere.

questions.question: The species that _______ a bare area are called pioneer species.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**invade.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pioneer species are the first organisms to colonize a newly formed or disturbed area.**
 
• These species are able to survive in **harsh conditions and are usually fast-growing and hardy.**
 
• The sequential, gradual, and predictable changes in the species composition in an area are called succession or ecological succession.
 
• The **entire sequence of communities that successively changes in a given area is called sere(s).**
 
• The individual transitional communities are termed seral stages or seral communities.
 
• The community that is in near equilibrium with the environment is called a climax community.
 
• The species that invade a bare area are called pioneer species.​

**Explanation:**

 
• **Lichens are the pioneer species on a bare area or Xerarch condition.**
 
• The lichen secretes some acids to dissolve rock and help in weathering and soil formation.
 
• Later, some small bryophytes invade and hold a small amount of soil.
 
• The **bryophytes are succeded by herbs, shrubs, and ultimately big trees.**
 
• At last, a stable climax forest is formed.
 
• The xerophytic habitat gets converted into a mesophytic one.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: How is the vegetation affected by construction of large dams?

options.text: The plants produce nodules to produce nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
Vegetation gives rise to oxygen under aerobic conditions.
The growth of fungus is a lot
The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The construction of large dams leads to the flooding of vast areas, which results in the submergence of vegetation and the subsequent rotting of submerged plants under anaerobic conditions.**
 
• This rotting vegetation gives rise to large **amounts of methane,** which is a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming.
 
• **The loss of vegetation** due to dam construction also affects the biodiversity of the area**, leading to the displacement of wildlife and changes** in the local ecosystem.
 
• ** In some cases,** the construction of dams may also lead to the fragmentation of habitats and the **loss of connectivity between different areas, further impacting vegetation and wildlife.**
 
• **The production of nodules** by plants to produce **nitrogen-fixing bacteria **is not directly related to the construction of large dams and is not have a significant impact on dam construction on vegetation.
 
• ** While vegetation does **produce oxygen under aerobic conditions, this is** not a direct impact of dam construction on vegetation.** The submergence and rotting of vegetation under anaerobic conditions is the primary impact of dam construction on vegetation.
 
• **The growth of fungus **may be a secondary impact of the rotting of submerged vegetation, but it is not a direct impact of dam construction on vegetation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Large dams** have a significant impact on the environment, **including vegetation, wildlife, and local communities.**
 
• **The submergence of vast areas** of land and the subsequent flooding can lead to the** displacement of people and wildlife, changes in local ecosystems, and the loss of biodiversity.**
 
• **The production of methane** due to the rotting of submerged vegetation is a significant contributor to global warming and climate change.
 
• The construction of dams may also have social and economic impacts on local communities, including the loss of livelihoods and cultural heritage.

questions.question: A dense mass of water drops on smoke or dust particles in the lower atmosphere layers is referred to as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**smog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Smog is a type of intense air pollution.
 
• It is composed of smoke and fog which is why it is called "smog".
 
• Smog is formed when sunlight reacts with pollutants like nitrogen oxides and at least one volatile organic compound (VOC) in the atmosphere.
 
• Smog is common in industrial areas and cities with a lot of vehicular traffic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mist**

 
 
• Mist consists of small droplets of water suspended in the air.
 
• It is typically created when warm, moist air meets sudden cooling.
 
• Mist is less dense than fog and visibility is generally clearer than in fog conditions.
 
 
 
• **Blizzard**
 
 
• A blizzard is a severe snowstorm characterized by strong sustained winds of at least 35 mph (56 km/h).
 
• It typically lasts for a prolonged period—typically three hours or more.
 
• Blizzards can cause whiteout conditions and significant snow accumulation.
 
 
 
• **Frost**
 
 
• Frost refers to a thin layer of ice that forms on solid surfaces when the temperature drops below freezing.
 
• It typically occurs in clear, calm conditions where there is a loss of radiative heat.
 
• Frost can damage crops and other plants.

questions.question: Bawris are traditionally used for:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Bawris** are traditional stepwells primarily used for **storing and recharging groundwater**.
 
• They are **architectural marvels** designed to tackle water scarcity in arid regions, particularly in India.
 
• These structures not only serve as water reservoirs but also **help in maintaining the water table** in the surrounding areas.
 
• They are often intricately designed and have historical and cultural significance, dating back to ancient India.
 
• Bawris are particularly common in **Rajasthan and Gujarat**, where water scarcity is a significant issue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stepwells**

 
 
• Also known as **baolis** or **vavs**, these structures are unique to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• They were used not only for water storage but also as places for social gatherings, religious ceremonies, and resting spots.
 
• Stepwells are often multi-storied structures with intricate carvings and artworks.
 
• They are an excellent example of ancient water management systems in India.
 
 
 
• **Water Conservation**
 
 
• Traditional methods like bawris play a crucial role in contemporary water conservation strategies.
 
• Reviving and maintaining such structures can help in sustainable water management.
 
• They are eco-friendly and do not require modern technology or electricity to function.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Significance**
 
 
• Many bawris are considered architectural masterpieces and are protected heritage sites.
 
• They showcase the engineering skills and aesthetic sense of ancient Indian civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Revival Projects**
 
 
• Several initiatives are underway to restore and preserve these historic stepwells.
 
• Community involvement is crucial for the successful revival and maintenance of these structures.

questions.question: What is the basic requirement for an ecosystem to function and sustain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Input of solar energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Solar energy** forms the **foundation **of the **food chain**.

 
 
• Plants, through the process of **photosynthesis**,** use solar energy** to **convert water and carbon dioxide into organic matter** (food).
 
 
 
• It is the** basic requirement** for an **ecosystem **to **function **and sustain itself.
 
• This organic matter serves as the primary energy source for all other organisms in the ecosystem, either directly through herbivory or indirectly through other **trophic levels (predation and decomposition)**.
 
• **Without **a constant** input of solar energy,** this **energy flow would cease**, leading to the **collapse of the ecosystem.**
 
• **Soil structure**, **organisms **(including plants and animals), and **micro-organisms** are all **crucial components of an ecosystem**, playing significant roles in nutrient cycling, decomposition, and maintaining the overall balance.
 
• However, **their existence and function ultimately depend on the continuous input of solar energy**.

questions.question: Which microscopic, single-celled photosynthetic organisms are known as the primary producers of the ocean - the organisms that form the base of the aquatic food chains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phytoplankton**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phytoplankton** are microscopic, **single-celled photosynthetic organisms** that are considered the primary producers of the ocean.
 
• They form the base of the aquatic food chains, supporting a wide range of marine life from tiny zooplankton to large whales.
 
• These organisms use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen through the process of photosynthesis.
 
• Phytoplankton are crucial for the marine ecosystem as they generate approximately half of the Earth's oxygen and serve as a major sink for carbon dioxide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zooplankton** are heterotrophic and feed on phytoplankton and other small organisms; they are not primary producers.
 
• **Bacterioplankton** consist of bacteria that play a role in recycling nutrients in the marine environment, but they are not primary producers.
 
• **Virioplankton** are viruses that infect marine organisms, including bacteria and plankton; they do not contribute to primary production.
 
• Phytoplankton populations are influenced by factors such as light availability, nutrient levels, and water temperature.

• A food chain shows how energy is passed from the sun to producers, from producers to consumers, and from consumers to decomposes such as fungi.

• Producers belong to the first trophic level, herbivores (primary consumers) to the second, and carnivores (secondary consumers) to the third. The important point to note is that the amount of energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

__
 
• **Deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystems exist at depths exceeding 1,000 meters on the ocean floor.**
 
• These ecosystems feature **hydrothermal vents, fissures in the Earth's crust, emitting hot, mineral-rich fluids **into the surrounding seawater.
 
• Vents are formed by **tectonic and volcanic processes**, releasing heated water containing high mineral concentrations.
 
• Life in these extreme environments includes bacteria, archaea, and specialized organisms **adapted to high pressure, darkness, and temperature fluctuations.**
 
• Unique microbial communities thrive around vents, utilizing **chemosynthesis **to produce organic matter from inorganic compounds.
 
• Hydrothermal vent ecosystems support diverse life forms such as **tube worms, clams, shrimp, and octopuses.**
 
• They contribute to global **biogeochemical **cycles and offer insights into the origins of life on Earth and potential extraterrestrial habitats.

• An **ecosystem is the basic ecological unit **in which living organisms interact among themselves and with their surrounding physical environment.
 
• **Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem**, the sun (sunlight) is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on earth.

questions.question: The condition when the amount of dissolved oxygen in a water body is alarmingly decreased is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hypoxia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypoxia** refers to the condition where the amount of **dissolved oxygen** in a water body is alarmingly low, making it difficult for aquatic life to survive.
 
• This typically occurs in areas where there is an excess of **organic pollutants or nutrient enrichment**, leading to phenomena like **eutrophication**.
 
• The lack of oxygen is harmful to aquatic organisms such as **fish, invertebrates, and plants**, which depend on oxygen for survival.
 
• Hypoxia is commonly observed in areas termed as **"dead zones,”** such as the Gulf of Mexico, where oxygen levels are insufficient for sustaining marine life.
 
• The primary causes include **agricultural runoff** (rich in fertilizers), **industrial discharge**, and **sewage effluents**.
 
• It is a critical environmental issue as it disrupts the **aquatic ecosystem**, affects biodiversity, and has economic implications for fisheries.
 
• Prevention and mitigation strategies include reducing nutrient pollution, improving wastewater treatment, and promoting sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hypothermia**__

 __
 
• **Hypothermia** is a medical condition where the body loses heat faster than it can produce, leading to an abnormally low **body temperature.**
 
• It is caused by prolonged exposure to **cold temperatures** and can result in fatigue, confusion, and in severe cases, organ failure or death.
 
 
 
• **Anoxia**__
 __
 
• **Anoxia** is the complete absence of **oxygen** in a given environment, often leading to the death of organisms.
 
• It is more severe than hypoxia and can occur in both aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Acidification**__
 
 
• **Acidification** refers to the process where water bodies become more acidic due to the absorption of **carbon dioxide (CO2)** or other pollutants.
 
• This phenomenon, commonly termed **ocean acidification**, has detrimental effects on marine life, particularly on organisms with calcium carbonate shells or skeletons.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about eutrophication is correct?

options.text: It happens when too less nitrogen is present in the water, causing reduced growth of plants and algae.
It is a beneficial process for environment restoration.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is a process where water bodies become enriched with nutrients, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus.
 
• This nutrient enrichment leads to **excessive growth of algae and aquatic plants**, which can result in harmful algal blooms.
 
• These algal blooms can deplete oxygen levels in the water, causing **dead zones** where aquatic life cannot survive.
 
• The primary sources of nutrients causing eutrophication include agricultural runoff, wastewater discharge, and industrial effluents.
 
• Eutrophication can lead to a loss of biodiversity, changes in species composition and dominance, and overall deterioration of water quality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preventive measures** include reducing nutrient runoff through better agricultural practices, improving sewage treatment facilities, and implementing policies to control industrial discharges.
 
• Restoration efforts for eutrophic water bodies may involve **mechanical, chemical, or biological methods** to remove excess nutrients and restore ecological balance.
 
• Public awareness and education about the sources and impacts of eutrophication are crucial for long-term water quality management.
 
• International cooperation and regulations, such as the European Union's Water Framework Directive, play a vital role in addressing transboundary water pollution issues.

questions.question: The increased concentration of suspended solids in water and their accumulation on bottoms where they are undesirable, creates what kind of water pollution?

__
 
• **Siltation** refers to the process by which fine particles like silt and sediment accumulate in water bodies, leading to pollution and degradation of aquatic ecosystems.
 
• This type of pollution occurs due to activities like **deforestation, mining, and construction** that increase erosion and sediment runoff.
 
• Siltation can disrupt aquatic habitats by **blocking sunlight penetration**, reducing oxygen levels, and smothering organisms living on the seabed or riverbed.
 
• It also affects water quality and can **reduce the capacity of reservoirs, lakes, and rivers**, impacting human activities such as irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• Preventive measures include **soil conservation practices**, afforestation, and the use of sediment control techniques to reduce erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suspended solids:**

 
 
• They are small solid particles that remain in water due to turbulence or slow settling rates.
 
• Sources include agricultural runoff, industrial discharge, and urban stormwater.
 
• Excessive suspended solids can lead to turbidity, reducing light penetration and affecting aquatic photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Impact of siltation:**
 
 
• Damages aquatic ecosystems by burying habitats and reducing biodiversity.
 
• Causes economic losses by reducing the efficiency of water infrastructure such as reservoirs and dams.
 
• Can lead to increased flooding due to reduced channel capacity.
 
 
 
• **Soil erosion:**
 
 
• A major contributor to siltation, caused by deforestation, overgrazing, and improper land management.
 
• Erosion control measures include terracing, planting vegetation, and using sediment barriers.
 
 
 
• **Other types of water pollution:**
 
 
• **Thermal pollution:** Caused by the discharge of heated water, impacting aquatic life.
 
• **Microbiological pollution:** Involves harmful pathogens entering water, affecting human and animal health.
 
• **Nutrient pollution:** Excess nitrogen and phosphorus lead to eutrophication, depleting oxygen levels in water bodies.

• The benthic zone is the ecological region at the **lowest level of a body of water**.
 
• It starts at the shoreline and continues down until it reaches the floor, encompassing the sediment surface and subsurface layers.

• Tiny, microscopic benthic organisms live in this zone and act as a source of food for bottom-feeding animals.
 
• Benthic organisms are very important as they are good indicators of water quality.

• Also, the filter feeders that live in this zone, such as mussels, are responsible for removing pollutants and sediments suspended in the water.
 
• **By contributing to nutrient cycling and pollutant and sediment removal, benthos is directly responsible for maintaining healthy water quality**.

__
 
• **Khadians** are traditional water-harvesting systems found in the arid regions of Jaisalmer, Rajasthan.
 
• These structures are designed to harvest and store rainwater for use during dry periods.
 
• Khadians are typically shallow wells or ponds that collect surface runoff from nearby catchment areas.
 
• This system helps in recharging groundwater levels and ensures the availability of water for drinking and irrigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guls**

 
 
• Guls are traditional irrigation channels used in the hilly regions of northern India.
 
• They are designed to divert water from streams and rivers to agricultural fields.
 
• These channels help in the efficient distribution of water across terraced fields.
 
 
 
• **Johads**
 
 
• Johads are small earthen check dams found in the state of Rajasthan.
 
• They are constructed to capture and store rainwater for recharging groundwater and providing water for agriculture and drinking.
 
• Johads play a vital role in improving the water table in arid and semi-arid regions.
 
 
 
• **Kuls**
 
 
• Kuls are water channels found in the mountainous regions of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
